{"id":"mimid-75nk","title":"Provider authentication: DNS-key RFC 9421 signatures, DANE, PKIX mTLS, trust lists, and Agora-style DID manifests","description":"Mark (2026-11-13): mimid implements every provider-authentication mechanism in the held mimi-protocol trust-anchor issue (IETF notes/2026-11-13-mimi-protocol-issue-mtls-trust-draft.md), plus Agora's relay mechanisms. That makes mimid the testbed where they're interop-tested against each other.

REVERSES decision mimid-1wgh.17 ('Inter-provider auth: none (early-email model)', 2026-10-17). Update that decision bead and AGENTS.md 'Known weaknesses that are deliberate' (and the main.rs # Limitations and README) once this lands, so nobody restores the old behaviour.

Mechanisms:
1. DNS-published keys plus RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures (the proposed MIMI default, DKIM-style): a <selector>._mimi.<domain> TXT key record, Ed25519, signing @method, @target-uri, content-digest (RFC 9530), created, and a source-domain field. Server-only TLS. Works without DNSSEC; stronger with it.
2. DANE for mutual TLS (draft-ietf-dance-client-auth): TLSA for the client certificate, DNSSEC required. Use ~/PROJECT/PKIX pkix-dane and pkix-dane-resolver.
3. PKIX mutual TLS for providers whose CAs issue clientAuth certificates (US Federal PKI, enterprise and private CAs): RFC 5280 path validation against configured trust anchors with policy constraints, and a dNSName match per RFC 9525. Use ~/PROJECT/PKIX pkix-path, pkix-identity, pkix-truststore and pkix-revocation; don't reimplement path validation in mimid.
4. Manual trust lists: configured peer keys, CAs or certificates per peer domain. This replaces the current peer map's lack of authentication.
5. Agora-style DID manifests (as local policy, mechanism-4 territory in the MIMI issue): a did:web or did:webvh identity, a signed manifest at a well-known URL with key status (active, deprecated, revoked), RFC 9421 with a DID URL as keyid, graduated trust levels and blocklisting, and 48-hour rotation overlap. Source: agora-spec spec/10-relays.md §10.1, §10.2.1, §10.2.3, §10.2.6. Bonus: Arkret coland uses DID-keyed RFC 9421 signatures, so this narrows the gap to coland (mimid-1wgh.46.11.2).","design":"PLAN (draft 2026-11-13, awaiting Mark's approval; sub-issues filed only after approval)

A. Architecture (mimid-server)
- An inbound ProviderAuthenticator trait: given the HTTP request plus TLS session info (the client certificate chain, if any), it returns an AuthenticatedProvider (domain, mechanism, key or cert id) or a refusal reason. One implementation per mechanism, composed by a per-deployment policy: an ordered list of accepted mechanisms, with per-peer overrides.
- An outbound ProviderCredential: request signing (1 and 5) and client-certificate presentation (2 and 3). This replaces the socat client-cert proxy for mTLS. reqwest with a rustls client identity, kept behind the same trait.
- The authenticated domain MUST match the From domain (§4.1) and, for /notify, the room's hub (mimi-protocol#179 rule). One disposition event per refusal, at DEBUG (a correct refusal, per mimid-bfzm).
- TLS termination: today Caddy terminates TLS. Mechanisms 2 and 3 need the client certificate, so either mimid terminates TLS itself (rustls server with optional client auth) or the proxy forwards the verified certificate in a header from a trusted hop only. Decide; prefer mimid terminating TLS so verification isn't delegated.

B. Order of work
1. Mechanism 4 (trust lists) together with the trait. Smallest, and it immediately fixes 'no authentication'.
2. Mechanism 1 (DNS keys plus RFC 9421). The proposed MIMI default; also gives mimid's outbound signing.
3. Mechanism 3 (PKIX mTLS via ~/PROJECT/PKIX). It also covers Haven today, since Haven's mimi-hubd uses mTLS with a configured CA.
4. Mechanism 2 (DANE via pkix-dane). Needs a DNSSEC-signed test zone.
5. Mechanism 5 (Agora-style DID manifests). It reuses mechanism 1's RFC 9421 code and adds DID resolution, the manifest and trust levels.

C. Dependencies and crates
- RFC 9421: check for a maintained Rust crate first; if none fits, write a small, well-tested module (RFC 9421 Appendix B test vectors).
- DNS: hickory-resolver (DNSSEC validation for mechanisms 2 and 1-with-DNSSEC).
- PKIX: path or git dependencies on ~/PROJECT/PKIX crates. Check their licenses are compatible with Apache-2.0 first.
- did:webvh resolution: reuse whatever mls-didwebvh-credential or Agora work exists; check ~/PROJECT first.

D. Tests
- Per mechanism: accept the right identity; refuse a wrong domain, bad signature, expired or revoked key, missing DNSSEC where required, a chain to an untrusted anchor, and policy-constraint failures.
- Mixed-policy interop between two mimid instances with different accepted mechanism sets.
- Live: against Haven (mechanism 3 or 4) and our haven.reviewcommit.com; later coland (5).
- Secrets canary: no private keys or signatures in logs above DEBUG.

E. Spec follow-through
- What mimid learns goes into the held trust-anchor issue (record formats, signature components, error codes) as running-code evidence, per memory reference-not-only.
- Mechanism 5 stays local policy in mimid and is not proposed to MIMI (positioning note in the held issue).","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"epic","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-13T23:02:58.428775652Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-13T23:02:58.428775652Z","labels":["security","interop","design"]}

{"notes":"APPROVED by Mark 2026-11-15, with changes:
1. Scope: mechanisms 1-4 only (DNS-key RFC 9421, DANE mTLS, PKIX mTLS, trust lists). Agora-style DID manifests (5) DROPPED for now; the coland gap (mimid-1wgh.46.11.2) stays open.
2. TLS: support both: mimid terminates TLS itself (rustls, optional client certs), OR takes the client certificate forwarded by a configured trusted proxy (Caddy) on the local hop.
3. Order: trust lists (+ trait) -> DNS keys + RFC 9421 -> PKIX mTLS -> DANE.
4. Enforcement: refuse by default; per-peer 'observe' mode logs the failure and accepts, for rollout (Haven).
5. RFC 9421: own module in mimid, tested against RFC 9421 Appendix B; sfv crate for structured fields.
6. PKIX: git dependency on github.com/MarkAtwood/crate-pkix pinned to an exact rev (crates are Apache-2.0 OR MIT).
7. DNS-key format (provisional, follows the WG): <selector>._mimi.<domain> TXT "v=MIMI1; k=ed25519; p=<base64>"; keyid = selector; covered: @method, @target-uri, content-digest (RFC 9530), created, and the From header as the source domain. DNSSEC not required (plan default): accepted without, with whether it validated logged."}
